deterministic.summary: HV loss was the BMS under-voltage protection acting (protective response, not the origin). Open upstream explanations: SOC estimation / calibration error; Usable capacity far below the stated parameter; Current under-measured or load bypassing the sensor. The recorded data does not separate them. A weak cell cannot explain the whole incident on its own: the highest cell was also depleted (pack-wide decline larger than the cell spread), and the SOC accounting discrepancy is pack-level: a weak cell can be an additional contributor, not the whole explanation. No root cause is confirmed.

result.headline: Whole pack fell at constant 7.9 A until BMS under-voltage tripped HV; HV was then reclosed five times.
result.explanation: BMS under-voltage protection opened the contactors. Why the cells were so low is open: SOC drift, far lower usable capacity, or under-read current. This recording cannot separate them.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT battery.pack_current held 7.9 from t=0 to 2100 s (4201 samples)
evidence.shows: Steady 7.9 A load. About 4.6 Ah was delivered before cutoff, against 61.6 Ah promised by the SOC.

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.pack_voltage[pack] changed level for good at t=665.5 s: median 307.7 before, 278.6 after V (5820x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Pack-wide voltage decline. The highest cell fell 450 mV, more than the 260 mV spread at the trip.
Level 1 at 1453 s, level 2 at 1799 s, level 3 at 2100.5 s. Both contactors opened at the same time (lines 19-20). This is protection acting.

evidence.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=2394.5 s: 56.8 -> 1.2 % (step -55.6, 34.8x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: SOC followed counted charge, then was corrected by about 55 points only after the trip. Consistent with SOC overstatement.
Fifth HV reclosure. Each reclosure went to level 3 and opened again. The lowest cell reached 2.420 V, below the original 2.500 V trip.

checked.check: Order of events around the trip (events, read_lines)
checked.result: Fault level rose 1, 2, 3 from t=1453 s to 2100.5 s. Contactors opened with level 3 (lines 18-20). Under-voltage came first, so the order does not fit a contactor-first fault.
checked.about: Contactor, VCU or insulation event first

checked.result: The highest cell fell 450 mV against a 260 mV spread at the trip. Cell index 2 was lowest in 100% of samples, with steps of at most 1 mV. Rest rebound was recorded.
checked.about: Weak cell as the sole cause; sensing fault

checked.result: About 4.6 Ah delivered against 61.6 Ah promised. That implies SOC overstated by about 57 pp, usable capacity near 7.5 Ah, or current under-read by about 13.4x. charge_accounting PASS: SOC followed counted charge.
checked.about: SOC drift, low capacity and under-read current all fit equally

checked.check: Sequence check in the window 500 to 700 s (sequence)
checked.result: No signal left its baseline in order inside the window, so it gave no earliest sign for the level shifts at t=605 s and t=665.5 s (lines 79-80).
No earlier cases with a similar signature.
Telemetry cannot separate SOC estimation error, low capacity and under-read current. Documents or an independent measurement are needed. A safety hold applies to HV reclosure.
checked.about: SOC error vs low capacity vs current under-read

effects.why: The contactors opened because the BMS protection acted. This shows how HV was lost, not why the cells were low.

effects.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=2394.5 s: 56.8 -> 1.2 % (step -55.6, 34.8x its usual variation)
effects.why: A correction to the estimate after the alarm, not a new discharge.

effects.quote: GAP battery.capacity_parameter no samples from t=2400 to 3299 s (899 s; usual interval 0.5 s)
effects.why: The same gap appears on every series (lines 63-78) during HV-open periods. The recording does not show whether the logger or the BMS stopped sending.
Repeated reclosure then re-trip cycles (lines 25-58) are the BMS re-protecting the already depleted pack.

safety_findings.statement: Do not close HV or charge until every cell's rest voltage is assessed. The lowest cell reached 2.420 V while HV was reclosed, below the original 2.500 V trip.
The last reclosure discharged deeper than the original trip. Review the restart policy; no specification is available to judge it.
HV was closed 5 times after the protective shutdown at 2100.5 s (3309.0, 3379.6, 3469.4, 3541.0, 3606.7 s). Whether this was permitted is unknown without a restart policy.
All 5 closures ended in another protective shutdown within about 18 s. The BMS kept re-protecting a depleted pack, so reclosure is not a recovery.
The fault resets before each closure fall in recording gaps and are not shown. Who or what reset the fault is not in the data.

unknowns: The recording does not show which of SOC drift, low capacity or under-read current caused the shortfall.
Veyra did not run compare or window at 2094.5 s. The recording does not show who or what set current to 0 A at 2094.5 s, about 6 s before the trip.
BMS protection thresholds, delays and restart policy are unknown, so the trip and reclosure sequence cannot be judged.
